children: Kanohar Electricals returned to the stock market after a 16-year absence on Wednesday, with its shares making a positive debut but falling well short of the premium indicated by the grey market ahead of listing.
The transformer maker’s shares opened at Rs 685.50 on the NSE, 8.5 per cent above the IPO price of Rs 632. On the BSE, the stock began trading at Rs 672.05, marking a 6.3 per cent premium.

The debut marks Kanohar Electricals’ return to the listed market after it voluntarily delisted from the BSE, Delhi Stock Exchange and Uttar Pradesh Stock Exchange in 2010. The company had originally listed its shares on the three exchanges in 1995, with low liquidity and trading volumes cited as the reasons for the subsequent delisting.

The company’s Rs 1,055.7 crore IPO had generated substantially stronger expectations in the unofficial market. Shares were reportedly commanding a premium of more than 30 per cent over the issue price ahead of the listing. The actual debut, however, shows the gap that can exist between grey-market indications and the price discovered on the exchanges.
IPO Drew 90.6 Times Subscription

The strong investor demand during the IPO was nevertheless reflected in the subscription numbers. The issue was subscribed 90.59 times, receiving bids for around 105.93 crore shares against 1.17 crore shares on offer.

Qualified institutional buyers led the demand, with their portion subscribed 215.37 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 87.74 times, while the retail portion received 20.51 times subscription.

Kanohar Electricals had set the IPO price band at Rs 601-632 per share, valuing the company at around Rs 5,004.6 crore at the upper end. The company had also raised Rs 316.72 crore from anchor investors ahead of the issue.

Mahesh M Ojha, Vice President, Research & Business Development at Kantilal Chhaganlal Securities, said Kanohar’s in-house manufacturing and integrated capabilities could support quality control, execution efficiency and scalability as demand for transformers increases.
He pointed to investments in power transmission and distribution, renewable energy integration, railway electrification and grid modernisation as potential drivers of transformer demand.
Transformer Business Drives Revenue

Kanohar Electricals manufactures transformers and undertakes engineering, procurement and construction projects in the power transmission and distribution segment. It operates manufacturing facilities at Rithani and Gangol in Uttar Pradesh, with combined transformer manufacturing capacity of 19,200 MVA.
As of March 2026, the company had an order book of Rs 1,818.3 crore. Transformers accounted for 83 per cent of its FY26 revenue, while EPC contributed 16 per cent.
The company reported a 45.1 per cent increase in revenue to Rs 653.8 crore in FY26 from Rs 450.6 crore a year earlier. Profit for the year nearly doubled to Rs 129.7 crore from Rs 65 crore in FY25.
Fresh Capital To Fund Expansion

The IPO comprised a fresh issue of up to Rs 300 crore and an offer for sale of 1.19 crore shares by promoter entity K Sons Family Trust. At the upper end of the price band, the OFS was valued at Rs 755.7 crore.

Of the fresh issue proceeds, Rs 64.1 crore will be used for capital expenditure and infrastructure requirements, including machinery for the Gangol facility, expansion and automation of backward-integration facilities, solar power plants and electric vehicles used at manufacturing facilities.
Another Rs 155 crore has been earmarked for incremental working capital, with the balance intended for general corporate purposes.

The company, promoted by IIT alumnus Dinesh Singhal, operates across transformer manufacturing and EPC activities, allowing it to undertake turnkey projects involving substations and transmission lines.

Kanohar’s return to the public markets comes at a time when investments in India’s power infrastructure are driving demand for transformers and related equipment, placing its listed debut alongside established players in the sector including Hitachi Energy India, BHEL, Schneider Electric Infrastructure, CG Power and Industrial Solutions, Transformers & Rectifiers (India) and GE Vernova T&D India.
